statement.text:
Let $n$ be a positive integer. For a finite group $K$ and an automorphism $\varphi$ of $K$ of order dividing $n$, let $$ X_{n,\varphi}(K):=\{x\in K\mid x x^{\varphi}\cdots x^{\varphi^{n-1}}=1\}. $$ Let $c_n$ be the supremum of the ratios $|X_{n,\varphi}(H)|/|H|$ over all finite groups $H$ and their automorphisms $\varphi\in\operatorname{Aut}(H)$ such that $\varphi^n=\operatorname{id}$ and $X_{n,\varphi}(H)
e H$. (a) Let $n>1$ be a positive integer such that $c_d<1$ for all prime power divisors $d$ of $n$. Is it true that $c_n<1$? (b) For a finite group $G$ and a positive integer $n$, the generalized Hughes--Thompson subgroup is defined as $H_n(G)=\langle x\in G\mid x^n
e 1angle$. Suppose that $n$ is a positive integer for which there is a positive integer $k_n$ depending only on $n$ such that $|G:H_n(G)|\leqslant k_n$ for all finite groups $G$ with $H_n(G)
e 1$. Is it true that then $c_n<1$?
